text: Charles Ponzi, the financial wizard, said to have made more than nine million dollars in a few months, by dealing in postal coupons.
His promise: fifty per cent profit in forty five days. Crowds handed him their savings.
His secret, he said, was postal reply coupons. Bought cheap in Europe. Cashed for more at American post offices.
But on page three, the same story quoted the Boston postmaster. In three months: thirty dollars worth of coupons, for Ponzi's company.
Two weeks later. Ponzi is arrested. Took in twenty millions. Says he cannot pay.
Nine million, as printed. Thirty dollars, as recorded. So where did the wizard's money come from? From the next investor in line.
